_meta.rules: verified=true means the source page or PDF was opened on the fetch date and the quote is present in the saved copy under data/raw/evidence/. access=abstract means only the publisher abstract (via Europe PMC) was opened. kind: measured = copied from a published source; reported = a figure a journalist reported from a study that is not published (no sample size, no method), shown as reported and never as measured; estimated = our arithmetic on measured figures (method given); assumption = set by us, editable.
_meta.sign_convention: In interventions.json effect values for metric days / relative_days are days SAVED (positive = faster). relative_days is the fraction of the interval removed. stage_shift_pp = percentage-point rise in stage I share. mortality_rr < 1 = fewer deaths.

source_study.description_en: Unpublished ongoing Finnish study of lung cancer treatment delays, coordinated by Professor Outi Kuittinen (University of Eastern Finland), run in Kuopio, Tampere, Turku and Rovaniemi. First results given to Yle MOT (published 12 Oct 2026). Sample size and whether figures are means or medians are not stated in the article text ("keskimäärin").
source_study.sample_size_note: Not stated in the article text; the infographic could not be read as text.
source_study.quote: Onkologian professori Outi Kuittinen Itä-Suomen yliopistosta koordinoi käynnissä olevaa tutkimusta keuhkosyöpähoitojen viiveistä. Sitä tehdään Kuopiossa, Tampereella, Turussa ja Rovaniemellä.

total.quote: Ylen MOT kertoi, että syövän hoidossa takamatka länsinaapureihin on pitkä. Tanskassa keuhkosyöpäpotilas pääsee hoitoon 67 päivässä. Ruotsissa viive ensimmäisten oireiden toteamisen jälkeen on 107 päivää. Suomessa viive on pisin, 155 päivää.
total.note: 155 days is stated in the Yle follow-up article (and the MOT infographic); the MOT article text says "keskimäärin noin viisi kuukautta". lo = 50+41+58; hi is our assumption.

patient.quote: Tutkimuksen perusteella potilaasta itsestään johtuva viive on yli 50 päivää, perusterveydenhuollossa kuluu 41 päivää ja erikoissairaanhoidossa 58 päivää.
patient.method: Source says "over 50 days". 56 = 155 total - 41 primary care - 58 specialist care. lo = 50 (stated floor), hi = assumption.
patient.definition: first symptom -> first primary care contact ("potilaasta itsestään johtuva viive")

primary.quote: Tutkimuksen perusteella potilaasta itsestään johtuva viive on yli 50 päivää, perusterveydenhuollossa kuluu 41 päivää ja erikoissairaanhoidossa 58 päivää.
primary.method: Point value from source. No interval published; lo/hi = +-20 % assumption.
primary.definition: time spent in primary care before referral ("perusterveydenhuollossa kuluu 41 päivää")

referral.quote: For specialist consultation after initial visit to a GP (weeks)                          2–4       1–2       1–2      1–2       2–3
referral.method: Yle MOT gives one figure for specialist care (58 days). No opened source gives a measured Finnish split of it. We split 58 days in proportion to three published Finnish figures that describe the same three sub-steps but do not add up to 58: GP visit -> specialist consultation 2-4 weeks (mid 21 d, Khalife 2025 survey mode), specialist consultation -> diagnosis 4 weeks (28 d, Khalife 2025), diagnosis -> treatment start 36-38 days (37 d, Finnish Cancer Registry 2018-2022 via IHE 2026). Weights 21:28:37 -> 14, 19, 25 days. lo/hi use the Khalife range for referral (2-4 weeks scaled) and +-30 % for the others. The unscaled figures sum to 86 days, i.e. the specialist phase may be longer than the 58 days Yle reports.

curative_access.note: v3. Used to turn "extra patients treated with curative intent" into deaths avoided. The conversion is an assumption, not a causal estimate; the sources below are context for its size.

deaths_avoided_per_extra_curative_patien.definition: deaths within five years avoided per additional patient who gets curative-intent treatment instead of none or non-curative treatment
deaths_avoided_per_extra_curative_patien.basis: The patients a county adds at the margin are older and less fit than those already treated, and some would have been cured anyway by later treatment, so the full difference between treated and untreated groups must not be used. Context: stereotactic radiotherapy in medically inoperable stage I patients gave 40 % five-year survival (RTOG 0236) against 6 % in untreated stage I patients (population registry, not a comparison of like with like): a difference of 0.34. We count under half of that (0.15) and allow 0.05-0.30. Not adjusted for anything; observational sources.
